agencies.name: SF Muni (SFMTA)

rows.applies_to: both N Judah legs, if paying the driver
covers both N Judah rides (exactly 2 x $2.85, so it only wins if you take a third ride)

rows.ticket: Clipper inter-agency transfer credit onto Muni
rows.validity: $2.85 off an adult Muni fare when transferring TO Muni from another agency within 2 hours
rows.applies_to: the return N Judah ride after tapping off Caltrain on the same Clipper/contactless card
not relevant for a single trip

notes: SFMTA also lists a youth fare-free policy for riders 18 and under and Visitor Passport options ($15 / $35 / $47).

agencies.name: Caltrain
agencies.zone_note: Zones used here: boarding station SF (22nd Street / 4th & King) = Zone 1, alighting Sunnyvale = Zone 3, so this is a 3-zone trip.

rows.ticket: Adult One-Way, 3 zones (ticket machine or Clipper)

rows.applies_to: reference (only if you went on to Santa Clara / Lawrence)

rows.validity: unlimited same-day round trips in Zones 1-3
rows.applies_to: equals 2 x $8.50, so it costs nothing extra and is the safer buy if any leg might need re-riding

rows.validity: Caltrain Day Pass plus $7.50; the Caltrain part is valid to Zone 3
rows.applies_to: covers both Caltrain rides and unlimited VTA rides

notes: Payment: Clipper card, contactless bank card or wallet tap on and off, or ticket machines on the platform. Caltrain is proof-of-payment - there are no gates, but fare inspectors check tickets.
One-way tickets are valid for 4 hours in one direction, so the outbound and return tickets must be separate.

agencies.name: VTA (Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority)

rows.applies_to: not useful for two rides exactly $5.00 apart

rows.validity: all day; a Clipper contactless accumulator caps a day of VTA rides at $7.50

notes: VTA publishes route 55 as a 25/30-minute midday bus and asks riders to be at the stop 5 minutes early; all stop-level times are approximate.

day_totals.label: Cheapest realistic - Clipper or contactless end to end, adult
day_totals.assumption: Adult fare, tap onto Muni, buy Caltrain one-way on the same card so the Muni transfer credit applies, tap VTA twice (same card, same service day).

items.label: Muni N Bus, 5:15 AM from home
Caltrain SF Terminal -> Sunnyvale, one-way, 3 zones
Muni -> Caltrain inter-agency transfer credit applied by Caltrain
VTA 55, Sunnyvale -> Stevens Creek & De Anza
VTA 55, McClellan & Felton -> Sunnyvale (same day, under the $7.50 cap)
Caltrain Sunnyvale -> SF Terminal, one-way, 3 zones
Muni N Judah metro, 1:56 PM (more than 120 min after the first tap, so a new Single Ride)

day_totals.caveat: Children 18 and under ride Muni free, which removes the $5.70 Muni half of this total.

day_totals.label: Same rides, but no transfer credit (contactless card tap or a printed ticket)
day_totals.assumption: Useful if you do not tap the same Clipper card onto Caltrain, or if you buy a paper ticket: the $2.85 Muni credit is not applied.

items.label: Muni N Bus
Muni N Judah metro
Caltrain one-way 3 zones, both directions
VTA 55, two single rides

day_totals.caveat: $2.85 more than the first option; the credit is the only difference.

day_totals.label: All cash
day_totals.assumption: $3.00 per Muni ride paid to the operator, Caltrain one-way bought at a ticket machine ($10.00 for 3 zones), VTA $2.50 per ride.

items.label: Muni, two rides at the cash fare
Caltrain 3-zone one-way at a ticket machine, both directions
VTA 55, two rides

day_totals.caveat: The most expensive way to do this trip. $6.15 of it is the cash/ticket-machine premium.

day_totals.label: Pass variant - Caltrain 3-zone Day Pass instead of two one-ways
day_totals.assumption: Same rides; the day pass buys you a second chance if a connection is missed.

items.label: Muni, two Single Rides
Caltrain 3-zone Day Pass (no day-pass add-on needed for one rider)
VTA 55, two single rides

day_totals.caveat: Identical to buying two one-ways with a card, so the day pass is free insurance against a missed train on the outbound leg.

day_totals.label: VTA-Caltrain Day Pass variant (not recommended here)
day_totals.assumption: The combined pass is adult-only and only covers Caltrain Zones 1-3 plus VTA, which is exactly this trip.

items.label: VTA-Caltrain Day Pass (Caltrain 3-zone Day Pass plus $7.50)
Muni, two Single Rides (never included)

day_totals.caveat: Costs $5.35 more than the Clipper option and adds nothing for a single one-way pair of rides.

day_totals.label: Youth version (18 and under), same chain
day_totals.assumption: Muni is free for youth 18 and under, so the whole trip is 2 youth Caltrain fares and 2 youth VTA fares.

items.label: Muni youth
Caltrain youth 3-zone one-way, both directions
VTA youth 6-18, two single rides

day_totals.caveat: Bring ID that shows the date of birth; conductor checks on Caltrain.
